claims.text: The ball-milled starting powder is a BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder has a high defect density.
The ball-milled powder may contain oxygen contamination.
SPS at 900–1000 °C precipitates a continuous nanocrystalline intermetallic network at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary intermetallic network is rich in Ti, V, Fe, Co, and Al.
A chemical-potential gradient at 900–1000 °C drives refractory-element segregation to grain boundaries.
The segregated grain-boundary elements form a thermodynamically stable intermetallic phase.
The intermetallic network kinetically blocks outward diffusion of volatile Mg.
Blocking Mg diffusion prevents composition loss during densification.
The intermetallic network facilitates formation of a dense, adherent protective oxide barrier.
SPS in the proposed temperature window produces a fully dense bulk alloy.
Grain-boundary strengthening and precipitation hardening significantly enhance hardness.
The intermetallic network and stable passive film improve oxidation and corrosion resistance.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient diffusion and driving force for bulk formation.
Sintering below 800 °C produces porous, under-densified material.
Sintering above 1000 °C causes rapid Mg evaporation and composition deviation.
Mg loss above 1000 °C disrupts the stoichiometry required to form the stable intermetallic network and degrades mechanical properties.
An insufficient sintering time prevents formation of a continuous barrier network.
A parabolic oxidation rate law is consistent with surface-reaction limitation rather than diffusion control through a barrier.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis includes 1000 °C within the operative 900–1000 °C interval, whereas the conditions state that temperature must remain below 1000 °C. The status of exactly 1000 °C is therefore inconsistent.
